findings.reason: it adds to §3 the same carry-or-justify clause that §2/§4/§5 already carry for their helper machinery, which is the mechanism the sibling sections use to prevent a duplicate implementation.
findings.text: §3 `current.book` names only the entry function it replaces (`clipped_support_current_moments` in `clip_quadrature.py`) and carries no reuse ruling for the helper machinery it depends on (`clipped_support_quadrature:415`, `_quadratic_support_vertices`/`_quadratic_support_vertices_jvp:852-862`, `_integrate_field_polynomial:446`, `_integrate_current_polynomial:635`); §6 deletes only "the solver and booking authority in `forward_operator.py`" and says nothing about `clip_quadrature.py`, so the §3 node could reimplement quadrature the tree already owns

findings.reason: naming `ConstraintRecord` as the owner to extend keeps the row scale in one place, the same ownership rule §6 applies to every other mechanism (GMRES kernel, operand machinery, field-null kernels, labeller).
findings.text: §5 declares that "each constraint row's scale is declared with the row ... and recorded in the receipt" as new acceptance machinery, but `ConstraintPair` already holds `target`, `tolerance`, `scale` and `initial_unknown` (constraint.py:202/223/257) and surfaces them through `ConstraintRecord` (constraint.py:1843), whose docstring already states the row is scaled "by one declared scale" (constraint.py:877); the plan names no owner for the scale

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — four pure functions (`read`, `book`, `apply`, `fixed_point`) each hide a whole pipeline stage (null finding + axis-connected membership; exact-clip booking; compensated map; Newton-GMRES) behind one signature, and §6 keeps geometry and polynomial helpers as private dependencies rather than new surfaces.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 re-declares the constraint row scale as new machinery, but `constraint.py` already owns per-row target/tolerance/scale.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the only surface the sections add is the `TopologyPolicy`/`SolvePolicy` operands, each stated as "carried by the existing `ForwardSolvePolicy` ... extended rather than duplicated", and §6 names the retirement (promotion ladders, frozen/live split, live-read fallback, active-set and anderson/reduced-Newton/chord routes, `fixed_point.py`, `reduced_newton.py`), so the added operands are accounted for by a named merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 is the only one of §2–§5 whose section text names no reuse candidate for the helper machinery it will sit beside, while §2/§4/§5 each carry a cite-or-justify carry ruling.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every replacement states why the existing mechanism cannot be extended: §4 "replaces the map ForwardFluxOperator performs today rather than wrapping it", §2/§5 "extended rather than duplicated".
